requirements.requirement: Trusted hosts (lan-a/node2) keep full access to guest hosts (lan-b/node3) in the trusted->guest direction
requirements.summary: Ping and TCP connect from node2 (trusted) to node3 (guest) succeeded after routing was corrected (cmd-d87a2e9b7ce64c3b, cmd-9d3d8628701b417a), and this was re-verified after node1's restart (cmd-60d752c2555748be), after node2's restart (cmd-65e29ce286134509), and again after all three nodes had restarted (cmd-2d9e31863d6d4340).

requirements.requirement: No host on lan-b (node3/guest) may open a connection to any host on lan-a (node2/trusted)
requirements.summary: Both ICMP ping and TCP connect attempts from node3 to node2 failed/blocked consistently before any restarts (cmd-6fa9fdcbc6b3467e, cmd-2ada140691dc4c8e), after node1's restart (cmd-d0a8f202795d406c), and after node3's own restart (cmd-13e50dbb84934fa8), reflecting the guest-zone forward=REJECT firewall policy on node1.

requirements.requirement: Guests must still be able to reach services node1 itself offers, such as DNS
requirements.summary: node3 successfully connected to node1's DNS service on its guest-facing IP (10.0.20.1:53) both immediately after configuration (cmd-6fa9fdcbc6b3467e, cmd-2ada140691dc4c8e) and after all node restarts (cmd-13e50dbb84934fa8), consistent with the guest zone's input=ACCEPT policy.

requirements.requirement: Network/firewall configuration on node1 (and static IP/route config on node2/node3) survives a reboot
requirements.summary: UCI config was committed (uci changes empty) prior to reboot (cmd-f2a7da983b784675) and confirmed intact with correct interface IPs and firewall zone/forwarding rules after node1's restart (cmd-c5a9da4c4e284820, cmd-cd91fa551a5444ef); node2/node3 static IPs and routes in /etc/network/interfaces also survived their respective restarts (cmd-65e29ce286134509, cmd-13e50dbb84934fa8).

requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 9e75e4c2... captured while node1 was healthy (cmd-8450a711ca22487a); reboot triggered and acknowledged (cmd-9519a428a67347a8); SSH timeouts during the transition (cmd-3d6def6c17a34578); new boot_id 9b779ac7... observed on return (cmd-76fb06ea531e449b); firewall/network config and isolation policy re-verified working post-restart (cmd-c5a9da4c4e284820, cmd-d0a8f202795d406c, cmd-60d752c2555748be).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 66da71d8... captured while healthy (cmd-d59f8e1bd87241a1); reboot triggered (cmd-1a4a3b539d2b44e7); connection reset/timeout cycle observed during transition; new boot_id 9b621e57... confirmed (cmd-098f533c362b4160); eth1 static IP, route, and trusted->guest connectivity re-verified post-restart (cmd-65e29ce286134509). Matches the fixed after-executor snapshot boot_id 9b621e57..., differing from the before-prepare snapshot 66da71d8..., independently confirming the transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, observed evidence: node1's OpenWrt firewall enforces trusted(node2)->guest(node3) full access while blocking all guest->trusted connections (ping and TCP), guests retain access to node1's own DNS service, and the configuration survives reboot. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor snapshots), and re-verified recovered state and isolation policy after each restart and after all three restarts combined.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare-to-after_executor diff.

Node1's after_executor boot-identity observation itself returned a connection failure (return_code 255) at the moment of that fixed snapshot capture, slightly after the executor's own final restart-recovery checks succeeded; this is not treated as contradicting the executor's direct restart evidence since it's plausible transient timing, but it is noted as a minor inconsistency in the fixed snapshot data.

DNS resolution for a specific hostname (openwrt.lan) returned NXDOMAIN in one guest test (cmd-6fa9fdcbc6b3467e), though TCP/UDP port reachability to the DNS service itself was consistently confirmed, so the 'service is reachable' outcome is still satisfied even though that particular lookup found no matching record.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were directly tied to building or verifying the isolation topology (UCI network/firewall config on node1, static IP/route config on node2 and node3, and the mandatory node-restart cycle). One iteration mis-step occurred: node2 and node3 initially had a default route added via the new eth1 interface (cmd-ee32967f124f47f3, cmd-523e7b0f46df43b6), which was promptly identified as wrong and removed/replaced with a scoped host route in the same session (cmd-0909d73ac815479b, cmd-1ef6ae4058244768, then finalized via cmd-f4d329732df54c75/cmd-871b344f7af64204) — a bounded, low-risk troubleshooting correction that was fully reverted and did not persist in final config. A minor unmanaged mutation is a backgrounded `nc -lu -p 53` diagnostic listener started on node1 (cmd-7c660bd2954b4384) to probe port usage; it was not part of the final solution and there is no evidence it was subsequently killed or cleaned up (though it likely failed to bind since dnsmasq already held UDP/53, per the process list in the same command). Multiple reboot-trigger retries on node1 (cmd-08ad16b3f47945b0, cmd-b246e518050d41f2, cmd-9519a428a67347a8) reflect earlier attempts failing to actually execute (missing disown/nohup on this busybox image) before succeeding — these were ineffective attempts rather than harmful mutations. Package-health and listening-socket diffs between before-prepare and after-executor snapshots are all explained by the intended topology changes (new dnsmasq listeners on 10.0.10.1/10.0.20.1, new boot-derived ephemeral ports) or by node restarts, with no signs of damaged package state or newly failed services.
